resources.string: Covers the \"Send to new group chat\" button in Instagram\'s share sheet so a group is never created by an accidental tap. Reads only the layout of that screen on your phone. Collects and sends nothing.

IG Group Guard uses the Accessibility Service API. It reads the layout of Instagram\'s share screen on your phone (button names and positions) only to find the \"Send to new group chat\" button and cover it, so a group is never created by an accidental tap. IG Group Guard does not read your messages or contacts, does not collect or store any personal data, and has no internet access, so nothing leaves your phone. You can turn it off any time in Settings > Accessibility.
IG Group Guard cannot work without this. Nothing was turned on. You can agree later from this screen.
If you already turned it on, Android may have stopped it (force stop or battery saver). Open Accessibility settings, switch IG Group Guard off and on again.
When you share a reel or post to several people, the \"Send to new group chat\" button is covered so a group is never created by accident. \"Send separately\" keeps working.

To turn it on: Settings > Accessibility > Installed apps (or Downloaded apps) > IG Group Guard > On.

Android 13 or newer: if the switch is greyed out, open Settings > Apps > IG Group Guard, tap the menu (three dots) and choose "Allow restricted settings", then try again.

Some phones stop background services to save battery. If the button comes back, set IG Group Guard's battery use to Unrestricted.
When I tap \"Send to new group chat\"
Ask me first: a popup asks whether you really want to create a group. If you choose Create group, the button works normally until you close that share screen.
Blocked: this would create a group with everyone selected. Use \"Send separately\".
Unlocked. Tap \"Send to new group chat\" to create the group.
This puts all %1$d people you selected into one new group, and they can see each other. To message each person on their own, choose Cancel and use \"Send separately\".
This puts everyone you selected into one new group, and they can see each other. To message each person on their own, choose Cancel and use \"Send separately\".
Bank or payment app will not open?

Some banking and payment apps refuse to start while any accessibility service is turned on. That is their security rule, not a fault in IG Group Guard. Pause IG Group Guard while you use them:
• Tap \"Pause for banking\" below, or • Add the IG Group Guard tile to Quick Settings (pull down twice, tap the pencil icon), or • Set the accessibility shortcut: Settings > Accessibility > IG Group Guard > Shortcut. Holding both volume keys then turns it on and off.
Some apps (for example Google Pay) require every downloaded accessibility app to be off, including launchers, and ask you to restart the phone afterwards. Turn IG Group Guard back on when you are done.
IG Group Guard paused. Your banking app can open now. Turn it back on in Accessibility settings, the tile, or the volume-key shortcut.
